name: Abishur
overview: Abishur was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Shammai. His identity is rooted in his lineage within the tribe of Judah, emphasizing his place in the genealogical records of Israel. Beyond his paternal connection, there are no additional notes detailing his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Abishur means '[my] father is a wall,' reflecting a possible symbolic meaning of protection or strength associated with his family. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Abishur as the son of Shammai. He is also inferred to be the husband of Abihail and the father of Ahban and Molid, showing his role as a patriarch within his family line. These relationships are documented in the genealogical listings of 1 Chronicles 2.
scriptureSignificance: Abishur's significance lies in his place within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Judah, contributing to the biblical record of Israel's ancestry. His lineage connects important family lines, which is vital for understanding the heritage from which Christ ultimately came. While not highlighted for specific deeds, his inclusion in Scripture underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant people through generations.
